title: Bronchoscopy, Sputum Induction & Sleep Studies Quiz

questions.text: What is bronchoscopy used to visualize directly?

answers.text: Pathologic changes in the trachea and bronchi
Only movement of a limb during rest
The number of apneas per hour without airway visualization

questions.text: Which finding is an indication for diagnostic bronchoscopy?

answers.text: Need to measure daytime alertness only
Abnormal chest X-ray, such as a mass

questions.text: Which pair is listed as the most common causes of hemoptysis?
Which is a therapeutic use of bronchoscopy?

answers.text: Estimating total sleep time by limb movement

questions.text: Which is an absolute contraindication to bronchoscopy?
Which bronchoscopy hazards account for the majority of deaths associated with the procedure?
What is the purpose of atropine before bronchoscopy?

answers.text: Reduce salivation, bronchial secretions, and vasovagal reflex

questions.text: Which medication is used to reverse Versed if the patient is overmedicated?
Overuse of benzocaine spray can cause which complication?
How long should the patient fast before bronchoscopy according to the lesson?
How is a cytology lavage specimen prepared?

answers.text: Saccomanno solution is added in a 50-50 mix
It is placed only in formalin
It is flushed only with Hank's solution

questions.text: Which foreign body removal device uses a single looped wire for long, thin objects?
What is the most common bronchoscopy approach listed in the lesson?
After bronchoscopy, how long should the patient avoid eating or drinking?
What is the purpose of sputum induction?

answers.text: Collect fresh, uncontaminated secretions from the tracheobronchial tree

questions.text: What may be administered by SVN when a patient has difficulty producing a strong productive cough?
Which test is required for definitive diagnosis of sleep apnea?
How is obstructive sleep apnea identified during interpretation?

answers.text: No respiratory effort detected and no airflow
Respiratory effort detected with minimal airflow only
Limb movement recorded for a week or more
Respiratory effort detected but no airflow

questions.text: What does AHI represent?

answers.text: The number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep
The number of REM entries during MSLT
The number of bronchoscopy biopsies per procedure
The number of oxygen desaturations during sputum induction

questions.text: Which therapy is first-line medical therapy for OSA according to the lesson?
Why may BiPAP be ideal for some patients?

answers.text: They require separate pressures for inhalation and exhalation
They need no airflow measured for 10 seconds
They need a sterile suction catheter connected to a trap

questions.text: What is overnight pulse oximetry used to determine?

answers.text: Whether a patient has bronchospasm from topical anesthesia
Whether treatment such as CPAP or BiPAP is effective

questions.text: What does actigraphy measure?

answers.text: Airflow at the nose and mouth

questions.text: Which MSLT finding supports narcolepsy in the lesson?

answers.text: Falling asleep quickly without REM sleep
Staying awake for 40 minutes in every trial
Entering REM sleep two or more times during the MSLT
No respiratory effort and no airflow

questions.text: Which statement correctly compares MSLT and MWT?

answers.text: MSLT uses four trials; MWT uses five naps
MSLT measures falling asleep and REM entry; MWT measures ability to stay awake
MSLT is for foreign body removal; MWT is for cytology specimens
MSLT ends at 40 minutes; MWT ends at 20 minutes
